title: Feelings & opinions
goal: Say how you feel, give and ask for opinions, agree and disagree, and link ideas with because, but and so.
intro:
This unit lets you go beyond facts: happy, tired, worried, bored; 'I think…', 'I don't think so', 'you're absolutely right'.

You'll notice two ways of expressing feelings: some are adjectives (**मैं ख़ुश हूँ** 'I'm happy'), while others are nouns that 'come to' you (**मुझे ग़ुस्सा आ रहा है** 'I'm getting angry'). And the most common way to give an opinion uses our old friend लगना: **मुझे लगता है कि…** 'it seems to me that…'.

grammar.title: Two ways to express feelings
grammar.body:
**1. Adjective + होना** — 'I am happy': मैं **ख़ुश** हूँ, वह **उदास** है, हम **परेशान** हैं. Most of these adjectives are invariable; थका, अकेला agree (मैं थकी हूँ, f).

Tiredness and boredom are often expressed as something that has happened: **मैं थक गया हूँ** 'I've got tired', **मैं बोर हो रहा हूँ** 'I'm getting bored'.

**2. Dative + noun + verb** — the feeling 'comes to' or 'strikes' you:

मुझे **ग़ुस्सा आता है** 'I get angry' · मुझे **शर्म आती है** 'I feel shy' · मुझे **मज़ा आया** 'I enjoyed it'
मुझे **डर लगता है** 'I'm afraid' · मुझे **अच्छा लगा** 'I liked it'
मुझे **चिंता है** 'I'm worried' · मुझे **उम्मीद है** 'I hope'

The verb agrees with the feeling-noun: ग़ुस्सा (m) **आया**, शर्म (f) **आई**. The cause takes **से** (कुत्तों से डर) or **पर** for anger (मुझे उस पर ग़ुस्सा आया 'I got angry at him').

grammar.title: Giving opinions: मुझे लगता है कि…
grammar.body:
The most natural way to say 'I think (that)…' is **मुझे लगता है कि…** — literally 'it seems to me that…'. Others:

**मेरे ख़याल से…** 'in my view…' · **मेरी राय में…** 'in my opinion…' (more formal)
**मैं सोचता/सोचती हूँ कि…** — correct, but sounds more like 'I'm thinking / I reckon' than a quick opinion.

Ask: **आपको क्या लगता है?** 'what do you think?'
Agree: **मैं आपसे सहमत हूँ** · **आप सही कह रहे हैं** · **बिल्कुल!** · **हाँ, सच में**
Disagree politely: **मुझे ऐसा नहीं लगता** 'I don't think so' · **मैं सहमत नहीं हूँ** · **शायद, लेकिन…** 'maybe, but…'

The word **कि** 'that' joins the opinion to the main clause. In careful speech it is kept, but after लगता है it is often dropped in casual speech: लगता है बारिश होगी 'looks like it'll rain'.

grammar.title: Linking ideas: क्योंकि, लेकिन, इसलिए, तो
grammar.body:
**और** 'and' · **या** 'or' · **लेकिन / पर / मगर** 'but' · **क्योंकि** 'because' · **इसलिए** 'so, that's why' · **तो** 'so, then'

They work much like English and come at the start of their clause:

मैं थका हूँ, **क्योंकि** मैंने बहुत काम किया।
मैं थका हूँ, **इसलिए** मैं घर जा रहा हूँ।

**तो** is extremely common in speech as 'so / well then', and also as an emphasis particle after a word: मैं **तो** ठीक हूँ 'I'm fine (at least)'. **पर** 'but' is the most common in conversation; **लेकिन** is neutral; **मगर** is a bit literary.

culture: Indians often express disagreement indirectly — 'शायद…', 'देखते हैं' ('we'll see') or a vague 'हाँ, हाँ' can politely mean 'no'. The famous Indian **head wobble** (a side-to-side tilt) usually means 'yes', 'OK' or 'I'm listening', not 'no'. Bollywood is a national conversation topic: films, songs and actors are safe, fun subjects with almost anyone. Strong emotions are expressed openly within families, but public displays of affection between couples are still frowned upon in many places.

lessons.title: How are you feeling?

tip.title: मैं ख़ुश हूँ — I'm happy
tip.body:
- Most feeling words are adjectives with **होना**: मैं **ख़ुश** हूँ, वह **उदास** है, हम **परेशान** हैं.
- ख़ुश, उदास, नाराज़, परेशान, हैरान never change; **थका** does: थका (m), **थकी** (f), **थके** (pl).
- Tired is often 'got tired': **मैं थक गया हूँ** (man), **थक गई हूँ** (woman).
- 'Upset with X' = X **से** नाराज़.

tip.title: मुझे डर लगता है — feelings that come to you
tip.body:
- Some feelings 'come to' or 'strike' you, so the person takes **मुझे / आपको**: मुझे **ग़ुस्सा आता है** 'I get angry', मुझे **डर लगता है** 'I'm scared', मुझे **मज़ा आया** 'I had fun'.
- The verb agrees with the feeling: ग़ुस्सा (m) **आता**, शर्म (f) **आती**.
- The cause takes **से**: पानी **से** डर.

lessons.title: What do you think?

tip.title: मुझे लगता है कि… — I think…
tip.body:
- 'I think (that)…' = **मुझे लगता है कि…** (lit. 'it seems to me that').
- Ask **आपको क्या लगता है?** 'what do you think?'
- Also **मेरे ख़याल से…** 'in my view', **मेरी राय में…** 'in my opinion'.
- **कि** 'that' joins the two parts — don't mix it up with **की** 'of'.

tip.title: क्योंकि, लेकिन, इसलिए
tip.body:
- **लेकिन** (or **पर**) 'but' · **क्योंकि** 'because' · **इसलिए** 'so, that's why'.
- They start their clause, just like in English: मैं थका हूँ, **इसलिए** घर जा रहा हूँ.
- **तो** 'so / well then' is everywhere in speech: **तो**, अब क्या करें?
